title: dsa-explain
section: A note on inspiration and attribution
text:
A note on inspiration and attribution
The idea of a free, visual, self-contained explainer for a technical topic owes a real debt to MLU-Explain, Amazon’s collection of machine-learning explainers (source on GitHub). We admire that project’s format: short, focused, one-idea-per-page lessons built around an interactive visual.
This site’s visual structure of navy-ink text and borders, flat/ sharp-edged cards, and a “highlighter” mark behind key text and buttons was deliberately designed to feel close to MLU-Explain’s. The accent color, though, is a deliberate departure: a cool cobalt blue rather than their warm coral/orange, chosen specifically so the two sites read as clearly distinct at a glance. No CSS, font files, illustrations, or written content from MLU-Explain were copied into this project: every rule in theme.scss was written from scratch, and the typefaces here (Archivo and JetBrains Mono) are open, freely-licensed Google Fonts chosen to evoke the mood of Amazon’s proprietary Ember typeface without using it. MLU-Explain’s own codebase remains under its own license — see the original, linked above, for the real thing.
Unless noted otherwise on an individual page, written content on this site is shared under CC BY-SA 4.0, and the site’s own source code (Quarto config, theme, and scaffolding) is available in the GitHub repository under the MIT license.
